sources.title: Günter Last and Mathew Penrose, Lectures on the Poisson Process (author-hosted 2017 monograph)
sources.locator: Chapter 4, Theorems 4.1 and 4.4 with their complete proofs, PDF pp.39–44; Chapter 8, Proposition 8.2, §8.2 Definitions 8.6 and 8.9, Propositions 8.7–8.8, Example 8.10, Proposition 8.11 and Exercises 8.10–8.12, PDF pp.81–87; §8.5 Theorem 8.14 and complete proof, PDF pp.89–92; Chapter 9 Theorem 9.1, Lemma 9.2, Definition 9.3, Theorem 9.4, and the Exercise 9.9 statement (PDF p.103; its proof is supplied locally); Appendix B.2 Theorem B.11 and complete proof, PDF pp.276–278.

contents.name: Chapter 4, Theorem 4.1: the single-point Mecke equation
contents.reason: The full finite-intensity and sigma-finite argument is reproved locally, including the one-occurrence deletion convention.

contents.name: Chapter 4, Theorem 4.4: multivariate Mecke equation
contents.reason: The assigned page proves only the single-point add-one/deletion identity; no multi-point insertion formula is claimed.

contents.name: Chapter 8, Proposition 8.2: mean measure of a stationary finite-intensity process
contents.reason: The mean-measure hypotheses and local-finiteness step are proved explicitly for the half-open unit cube convention.

contents.name: Chapter 8, Definition 8.6: reduced second factorial moment measure
contents.reason: The local definition makes the occurrence-indexed displacement convention explicit.

contents.name: Chapter 8, Proposition 8.7: local finiteness and disintegration of the reduced measure
contents.reason: The local theorem proves the forward local-finiteness direction and measurability needed here; it does not claim the converse or the full disintegration formula.

contents.name: Chapter 8, Proposition 8.8: equivalence with a full second-moment density
contents.reason: The page defines pair correlation through absolute continuity of the reduced measure and does not claim the equivalent two-variable density characterization.

contents.name: Chapter 8, Definition 8.9: pair-correlation function
contents.reason: The density condition is retained explicitly, and no density is presumed to exist.

contents.name: Chapter 8, Example 8.10: Poisson pair-correlation function equals one
contents.reason: The assigned Poisson result is K(r)=volume of the closed radius-r ball; it does not assert a pair-correlation density.

contents.name: Chapter 8, Proposition 8.11: small-window one-point probability limit
contents.reason: Small-set occupancy asymptotics are outside the assigned spatial-summary claims.

contents.name: Chapter 8, Exercise 8.10: simplicity iff no reduced-measure atom at zero
contents.reason: The page explains the origin multiplicity convention but does not claim a general simplicity characterization.

contents.name: Chapter 8, Exercise 8.11: conditional mean measure given the invariant sigma-field
contents.item: The local spatial-limit proof establishes the needed invariant-event integral identity directly, without importing this exercise as an unproved premise.

contents.name: Chapter 8, Exercise 8.12: a factorial-moment implication for scalar random variables
contents.reason: Local square integrability is an explicit hypothesis of the assigned factorial-measure result, so this auxiliary implication is unnecessary.

contents.name: Chapter 8, Theorem 8.14: spatial mean ergodic theorem for convex dilates
contents.item: The statement is in scope. The inspected source proof treats d=2 then leaves other dimensions to the reader, and its full-sequence liminf identification does not follow from convergence in probability; the local proof supplies a complete all-d proof and identifies the conditional expectation by invariant-event integrals.

contents.name: Appendix B.2, Theorem B.11: L1 mean limit for stationary integrable sequences
contents.reason: A complete choice-free proof is supplied locally and then used coordinate by coordinate.

contents.name: Chapter 9, Theorem 9.1: refined Campbell theorem and full Palm law
contents.reason: The local construction proves existence, uniqueness, and the origin-occurrence property from a sigma-finite Campbell measure.

contents.name: Chapter 9, Lemma 9.2: joint measurability of recentering
contents.reason: The local evaluation-kernel proof avoids a measurable enumeration of all point locations.

contents.name: Chapter 9, Definition 9.3: Palm distribution
contents.reason: The definition uses the full refined Campbell identity rather than conditioning on a null event.

contents.name: Chapter 9, Theorem 9.4: Mecke-Slivnyak characterization of the Poisson Palm law
contents.reason: The assigned theorem proves the forward homogeneous-Poisson Palm law needed for K by Mecke; the converse Poisson characterization is outside scope.

contents.name: Chapter 9, equation (9.6): equivalent uncentered Campbell form
contents.reason: The page states and uses the recentered full Palm identity and makes no separate uncentered Palm formula claim.

contents.name: Chapter 9, Exercise 9.9: reduced second factorial measure as one-occurrence Palm deletion
contents.reason: The local proof tracks distinct occurrence indices, so co-located points other than the distinguished point remain.

sources.title: Adrian Baddeley, Spatial Point Processes and their Applications (complete lecture notes)
sources.locator: Lecture 2, §§2.3–2.6, PDF pp.33–40: all named Examples 2.8–2.18, Theorem 2.4, Lemmas 2.1–2.2, and border-method equations (16)–(18); Lecture 3, §§3.2–3.3, PDF pp.44–50: Examples 3.3–3.8, Theorems 3.1–3.2, and Lemma 3.1, including the stated Campbell-Mecke and Palm reasoning.

contents.name: Lecture 2, Example 2.3: uniformly translated grid
contents.reason: The local example specializes the translation argument to a one-dimensional lattice and computes its atomic reduced measure and doubled multiplicity case.

contents.name: Lecture 2, Theorem 2.1: translation-invariant measure is a multiple of Lebesgue measure
contents.reason: A local face-null argument reconciles the half-open unit cube with the source normalization.

contents.name: Lecture 2, Theorem 2.2: Campbell formula
contents.reason: The refined Campbell identity contains this nonnegative-integrand formula as the constant-configuration special case.

contents.name: Lecture 2, Examples 2.8–2.12: Poisson, binomial, and cluster second-moment calculations
contents.reason: These process-specific variance and second-moment calculations are not needed for the assigned general Palm and spatial-summary statements.

contents.name: Lecture 2, Theorem 2.4: full two-variable reduced second-moment disintegration
contents.reason: The page defines and proves local finiteness of the reduced measure and the Palm identity, but does not claim this general disintegration formula.

contents.name: Lecture 2, Example 2.13: Poisson reduced second moment measure
contents.reason: The Poisson result on this page concerns K(r); it does not assert a full Borel-set formula for the reduced measure.

contents.name: Lecture 2, Example 2.14: integrate the pair-correlation density to obtain K
contents.reason: The item states the density hypothesis and integrates over the explicitly closed ball.

contents.name: Lecture 2, Example 2.15: translated square grid has atomic reduced measure
contents.reason: The assigned example verifies the same obstruction in one dimension and adds the occurrence-multiplicity distinction.

contents.name: Lecture 2, Example 2.16: homogeneous Poisson K-function is ball volume
contents.reason: The local proof derives this from the full-Palm law and one-occurrence Mecke identity, including r=0.

contents.name: Lecture 2, Example 2.17: K is the integral of the pair-correlation density
contents.reason: The local theorem proves the closed-ball form from the reduced Palm identity.

contents.name: Lecture 2, Lemma 2.1: radial derivative of K under planar isotropy
contents.reason: Isotropy, differentiability, and the derivative formula are not hypotheses or conclusions of this page.

contents.name: Lecture 2, Example 2.18: translated-grid lattice-point count formula for K
contents.reason: The assigned lattice example establishes atomicity and multiplicity but does not claim an explicit lattice-point counting formula for K.

contents.name: Lecture 2, Lemma 2.2: invariance of K under independent thinning
contents.reason: No thinning construction or thinning-invariance claim appears on the assigned pages.

contents.name: Lecture 2, equations (16)–(18): border correction and observation-window edge effect
contents.reason: The finite-data border formula is recorded as a procedure; the source bias discussion is not used to claim unbiasedness or asymptotic performance.

contents.name: Lecture 3, Example 3.3: homogeneous Poisson Palm distribution
contents.reason: The item proves the stationary homogeneous special case directly from the local Mecke identity.

contents.name: Lecture 3, Example 3.4: mixed-Poisson Palm distribution
contents.reason: Cox and mixed-Poisson Palm laws are outside the assigned scope.

contents.name: Lecture 3, Theorem 3.1: Slivnyak theorem
contents.reason: Only the homogeneous stationary Palm-law consequence required for the K calculation is proved here.

contents.name: Lecture 3, Examples 3.5–3.6: binomial and mixed-Poisson Palm distributions
contents.reason: These Palm laws concern process classes and conditioning conventions not claimed by the assigned pair.

contents.name: Lecture 3, Theorem 3.2: Campbell-Mecke formula
contents.reason: The local proof establishes both add-one and one-occurrence deletion forms for sigma-finite locally finite intensity.

contents.name: Lecture 3, Examples 3.7–3.8: dependent thinning and Boolean-model boundary length
contents.reason: Neither dependent thinning nor Boolean-model geometric functionals occur in the assigned claims.

contents.name: Lecture 3, Lemma 3.1: translation relation between location-indexed Palm laws
contents.reason: The page constructs the full Palm law at the origin but does not introduce a family of location-indexed Palm laws.
